x: It wouldn't fold back up properly
It'd be out of date before it was printed
f: "But if you're that lost, d'you know what I mean, forget the map..." Ricky cackled and clapped. Steve: "The map's not going to help you. Sure."
ex: They've made a map, haven't they? For the universe.
Well, yeah. As far as they can, yeah.
But if you're that lost, d'you know what I mean, forget the map...

q: Before Christmas, Karl 'tested' his mam by pointing out the Victoria Plum in a shop. What was her verdict?
a: "Oh, it's bloody awful."
x: "It looks a bit like your dad."
f: He'd already saved two weeks of paper round money to buy it. Ricky: "Oh Karl! I just- I- I- oh God!"
ex: So, uhh- so I saw it, I thought, "Yeah, she'll love that", right? So, I did me paper round, saved up for two weeks, right?

Got that sorted, went to Snips, bought the, uhh, Victoria Plum. Next day, I'm in- I'm in town with her, right. So I think, "Ahh, I know what I'll do!", I said, "Come- come in here a minute", right. S- uhh, so we go in and we're looking…
Oh Karl! I just- I- I- oh God!

q: In "What Price Karl", Karl agreed to shower with their mate Johnny for £1,000 (he wouldn't do £900). Why did he then pull out?
a: Ricky and Steve said they'd have to watch
x: He didn't want to get his hair wet
f: Ricky: "We said an we'll have to watch to make sure you do it. And he went no that's weird." Ricky later suggested leaving a DV camera in there instead.
ex: And he-and he went fine, he got-we got-he got a thousand pounds out of it, he wouldn't do 900, he got a thousand pounds out-but then, we said an we'll have to watch to make sure you do it.
And he went no that's weird.

q: What was Karl's simple plan for getting Rik Waller to lose weight?
a: His mam should buy less food and not get more if he eats it all
x: His mam should padlock the fridge
His mam should make him walk to the shops
His mam should only cook him salad
f: Steve called it "A short, sharp shop" and asked if Waller even lives with his mam. Karl: "I bet he does."
ex: So the thing is, right? Now with Rick, he lives at home with his mam. So why doesn’t his mam just say, “I’m going to buy less this week and if you eat it all, you’re not getting any more.”
Does he live with his mam?
I bet he does. I bet he does.
So you don’t actually know if this is true or not.

q: Karl told Steve that watching Ricky play football was like watching what?
a: A cat jumping on some wool you've thrown it
x: A walrus trying to get off a rock
A dog chasing its own tail
f: Karl said Ricky jumps on the ball and lies on top of it. Steve asked: "Are you sure he didn't just collapse from all the stress and the exercise?"
ex: Steve, have you seen Ricky play football?

It’s not football. It- you sort of do it like, um… it’s like when you get a cat and you chuck it some wool. You, sort of, jump on it and lie on top of it so you can’t get it and then, sort of, kick it with his feet, lying on the floor.
No, what I mean is he fouled me and I still, I was on--
Are you sure he didn’t just collapse from all the stress and the exercise?

q: Karl said Kate Bush's 'Babooshka', about a wife who disguises herself to seduce her husband, wouldn't work. Why not?
a: Suzanne can tell it's him down the high street just by the way he walks
x: Suzanne would know him by his voice straight away
Suzanne would smell his aftershave a mile off
Disguises only ever work in Scooby-Doo
f: Ricky pointed out: "You haven't even heard the song!" Karl's defence: "I'm controlling this feature."
ex: Nah, I don’t know what it is. We, we might as well start banging tambourines and urgggggggne. It’s ridiculous. This is rubbish. Right? But wait, some people e-mailed in…put him in a wheelie bin! Went to Blackpool! Right, erm, some people…
Just dismissed it like that. Why didn’t you think it would work?
Because you’d, you’d know, I mean, say like, say like, erm, right, Susanne right, who I go out with...
…right? She can see me from, say if I’m coming down the high street…

q: After hearing the second half of 'Living For The City', what did Karl guess the lad got arrested and 10 years for?
a: Not paying his bus fare
f: Karl was baffled: "He gets on a bus, all of a sudden some cop's arresting him." Ricky: "10 years!" Steve: "He got 10 years for that."
ex: …”They’ll sort of accept me as, y’know…and everything,” so he goes there and, er, the weird thing is he’s hardly, like, been in New York for a second…

…he gets on a bus, all of a sudden some cop’s arresting him, he’s like “What’s going on,” and he’s got 10 years, I mean. They didn’t…what you can’t hear, ‘cos the levels are quite bad I mean, I work with sound, I can’t really hear what’s…
I’m sort of guessing that he didn’t pay his bus fare or something, and er…

q: Introducing the show, Ricky gave Karl the credit for doing what?
a: Turned their microphones on
x: Made everyone a cup of tea
f: "Yeah! Exactly, and Karl, who's turned our microphones on." Steve: "Whay!"
ex: Xfm 104.9, Dandy Warhols, "Bohemian Like You". It's the Ricky Gervais Show.
Yeah! Exactly, and Karl, who's turned our microphones on.

q: In Karl's circus tale, why was a hippo sat right next to the trampoline?
a: It was getting ready to come on and do its act
x: It had escaped from the circus zoo
It was having its lunch break
f: Steve first assumed the hippo was sitting in the audience. Karl, laughing: "No, no!"
ex: But he was jumping and he was coming down and they're all going "Higher!" and he's going really high in the air, right. So he's- he's doing this, crowd are clapping. There's a hippo, right, just sat next to
The trampoline, getting ready to come on and do his act.
Oh right, I thought he was in the audience.
(laughing) This hippo getting ready to do his act, Steve!

q: When his school asked pupils to raise money for a local charity, what did young Karl decide?
a: Forget the charity, he was the charity
x: To give it all to a donkey sanctuary
To split it fifty-fifty with his mam
To put it towards a BMX
f: "I thought 'forget the charity'. I'm the charity here." Steve, laughing: "You're a charity?"
ex: No, what happened was, um, they did this thing at school about raising money for charity, right? For some local charity. And they said you can do anything to raise money and they came out with all these ideas and I thought that's good.
But forget... well, I dunno. I thought 'forget the charity'. I'm the charity here.
Yeah, it's just a good money-making... (laughing) You're a charity?

q: When Karl's gran died, his family inherited her pampered poodle Fluffy, which wore a little coat. What happened to it within a couple of months?
a: It became a wreck, covered in oil from going under the car
x: It got fat on Karl's dad's leftovers
It ran away back to his gran's house
It refused to eat anything but gran's cooking
f: Karl summed it up: "it went from being over treated to just being treated like a dog."
ex: It's called Fluffy. And like me gran looked after it in a way that it was treated like a human, do you know what I mean? And a little coat on when it went out, all that. Anyway, so she died. We get left it. My dad's like, oh, bloody hell.…
In the course of how long? A month?
Probably about two. Two months or something.
Now so it went from being over treated to just being treated like a dog.

q: Karl felt colour-changing chameleons were wandering out of their area. What was his public information advice to them?
a: Stay green, stay in the woods, stay safe
x: Stay still, stay quiet, stay alive
Go grey, go to town, go careful
Stay brown, stay low, stay home
f: Karl worried they'd wander "through a car park" turning the colour of concrete. Steve added: "Or into the colour of a Fiat Punto."
ex: No, but I just think we're encouraging them. You see, maybe this is evolution or whatever. But at the end of the day, because they can change color, they're wandering out of their area. They can be wandering about, you know, through a car…
Or into the colour of a Fiat Punto.
But they should just Stay green, stay green. Right. Stay in the woods and stay safe.
I love this public information words of advice for chameleons.
Stay green, stay in the woods, stay safe. Good night.

q: Karl's diary said some people in an old town still walk on all fours. What detail did he add that Steve didn't believe?
a: They wear shoes on their hands
x: They wear gloves on their feet
They eat their dinner off the floor
They sleep up in the trees
f: Karl's theory: "you only walk on two feet because you see everyone else doing it."
ex: Got up early, it's Suzanne's birthday. Gave her the card and present. She was well happy with her posh badge. She wore it to work. It's quite nice. Quite nice to hear a moment where she was actually happy for once. In your company. They…
That's not old fashioned. Why is that old fashioned?
That's some kind of regressive evolution.
It is true. It's somewhere in.
Well, I believe there are. They have found group people that are living and walking around on all fours. But I don't believe they're wearing shoes.

q: Karl confessed his shoplifting to his mam because his mate Antony's mam was coming round for "a word". What did she actually want?
a: To borrow 20 quid
x: To sell Karl's mam some raffle tickets
f: Karl: "She only wanted to borrow some money." By then he'd already owned up to nicking calculators and Mars bars.
ex: Confessed to nicking all this stuff... she comes 'round. She only wanted to borrow some money.
She said, "Oh... I don't like asking... I was a bit embarrassed to ask you over the phone but can I borrow 20 quid?"

q: At his brother's wedding (his brother was in the army at the time), why was the vicar getting "well annoyed" with Karl?
a: He sat in the car park all day playing a Ford Capri's musical horn
x: He kept ringing the church bells during the vows
He ran a raffle in the vestry during the service
He ate the wedding cake before the vows were done
f: Karl: "I just sat in that, doing that all day." That was during the service. It was also the last time he wore a suit.
ex: I didn't, I didn't really need to wear a suit, either, 'cause I didn't--I hardly went into the church, I was in the car park, right? And it was when me brother was in the army.
And he a Ford Capri with one of them horns that go, "Doo da doo doo, doo da doo da doo doo doo"--
Why didn't he, why didn't he come in his tank?
I just sat in that, doing that all day and the vicar was getting well annoyed with me.
What, when the service was on?

a: He's got Mondays off now
x: He's got his own parking space
He's been given a pay rise
He's got a chair with wheels

Yep. And he grasped that opportunity, didn't you? - by the horns. And three years later you're exactly where you started.....

q: Karl warned that meeting your girlfriend's parents gives you 'a little taster of what's to come'. What did he say about meeting Suzanne's mam?
a: It's a good job he didn't meet her early on
x: She's aged better than Suzanne has
She looks younger than he does
f: Ricky warned, "You're going to be in such trouble!" Karl's reply: "They don't listen, it's alright."
ex: It's that thing though innit of like, looking at her mam, there's a lot of truth in that isn't there? That you shouldn't really meet up with your girlfriends parents and that because you just sort of get a little taster of what's to come…
And what's to come with yours?
Erm...it's a good job I didn't meet her early on.
You're going to be in such trouble!
